vision.purpose: Build a software factory where agents create, verify, ship, observe, repair, and improve software with minimal human action.
vision.target: Agents complete most work without terminal care. Humans set intent, grant authority, amend rules, and review measured outcomes.
vision.humanRole: Humans write intent, approve spend, amend rules, and review exceptions and outcomes.
vision.systemRule: Keep durable context, explicit authority, independent proof, and replaceable service boundaries under every workflow.

workAuthority.name: Powder
workAuthority.description: Actionable work, claims, attempts, relations, activity, and proof records

items.title: Establish the project compass
items.outcome: Keep one concise repository view for vision, sequence, open decisions, research, and proof.
items.proof: The operator can find the vision, current item, and next items in less than two minutes.
items.question: Does one HTML projection give enough clarity before a roadmap service exists?
items.research: Compare small roadmap applications and test the view with a cold operator.

items.title: Make all agent work durable and asynchronous
items.outcome: Preserve runs, waits, replies, context, effects, cancellation, and recovery without terminal care.
items.proof: Stop a process or host. The correct run resumes at the correct wait without a duplicate effect.
items.question: Which substrate best preserves stable run identity, messages, waits, and cancellation?
items.research: Compare Temporal, Hatchet, Jujutsu workspaces, herdr, Agent Mail, Beads, Buzz, and direct message substrates.
coverage: Worktrees, Jujutsu, Buzz, IRC, and Beads

items.title: Test the specification pipeline
items.outcome: Turn signals into specifications and keep only workflow stages that improve measured results.
items.proof: Compare direct work with staged work across repeated tasks. Keep a stage only when it improves quality, time, or cost.
items.question: Which specification, plan, review, build, and end-to-end stages beat a direct frontier agent?
items.research: Run controlled comparisons across several task types, models, costs, and later reversals.
coverage: Human work at specification and PR review

items.title: Build an independent quality system
items.outcome: Combine deterministic gates, blind review, security checks, and useful evals without self-approval.
items.proof: Seed known defects and compare each judge with its null case. Keep only unique and stable detection.
items.question: Which independent judges detect useful defects at an acceptable cost?
items.research: Evaluate autoreview, Thermo reviews, Codex Security CLI, DeepSec, and seeded-defect benchmarks.

items.title: Compile fresh agent compositions
items.outcome: Select each role, model, tool, skill, context, authority, and verifier for one outcome.
items.proof: Reproduce a composition from its digest. Compare achievement prompts with a null prompt on repeated hard tasks.
items.question: Which composition and context choices improve results across repeated tasks?
items.research: Test model, provider, reasoning, skill, tool, context, and ambition-prompt choices on repeated hard tasks.

items.title: Join work, cost, proof, and outcomes
items.outcome: Link intent, run, composition, tokens, change, release, incident, proof, and later value.
items.proof: One query explains whether one change was worth its tokens and identifies every source record.
items.question: Which stable identifiers can Powder, R90, Canary, Overmind, OMP, and trace tools emit now?
items.research: Define shared identifiers and compare trace joins across current source systems.

items.title: Make failures loud and repair bounded
items.outcome: Connect each failure to its cause and start safe investigation, repair, rollback, or escalation.
items.proof: An injected failure starts a bounded response and keeps complete evidence without operator polling.
items.question: Which failures can agents repair without new authority?
items.research: Classify recent failures by detection, repair authority, blast radius, and required human decision.

items.title: Keep a user-persona fleet active
items.outcome: Run named user agents through real entry points and turn their evidence into product signals.
items.proof: Measure overlap between agent findings and later real-user findings. Change weak personas.
items.question: Which personas reveal important problems before real users report them?
items.research: Compare persona findings with support, analytics, incident, and real-user evidence.

items.title: Finish the full product surface
items.outcome: Treat documentation, change notes, onboarding, explanation, and distribution as product work.
items.proof: A new user can understand and adopt the product without operator guidance.
items.question: Which adoption evidence proves that a product surface is complete?
items.research: Test product understanding and adoption with cold users and user-persona agents.
coverage: Marketing sites, documentation, and change logs

items.title: Consolidate services around deep boundaries
items.outcome: Map functions before services, build where Misty Step has a thesis, and delete weak sketches.
items.proof: Each service boundary has one authority, failure, privacy, retention, or scale reason. Replaced projects leave no active path.
items.question: Which projects should become services, adapters, references, or deletions?
items.research: Compare current projects, provider tools, Ousterhout boundaries, build choices, and the separate Mint architecture decision.
